title: Understanding Parents' Complex Views of AI for Children's Pretend Play
abstract: arXiv:2609.39906v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: AI could support children's pretend play, but it could also direct the play on behalf of children. Whether AI should have roles in children's lives is controversial because its influence on children remains uncertain. We conducted semi-structured interviews with 10 U.S. parents, each with at least one child aged 4-15. During the interview, we described the concept of AI-supported pretend play and provided participants with two boundary-case storyboards. We analyzed the interview data through codebook thematic analysis, using inductive coding and affinity diagramming organized around the research questions, and then used qualitative systems mapping to examine relationships within and across themes. We found that the same characteristics of AI, e.g., ability to assume characters, responsiveness, and adaptability, were seen by parents as potentially useful but also concerning. Parents imagined that AI could make role-based play accessible

translated_title: 理解家长对人工智能用于儿童假装游戏的复杂看法
translated_abstract: 人工智能可以支持儿童的假装游戏，但也可能代替儿童来主导游戏。人工智能是否应该在儿童生活中扮演角色存在争议，因为它对儿童的影响仍不确定。我们对10位美国父母进行了半结构化访谈，每位父母至少有一个4至15岁的孩子。在访谈中，我们描述了AI支持假装游戏的概念，并向参与者提供了两个边界案例故事板。我们通过编码手册主题分析法对访谈数据进行分析，采用归纳编码和围绕研究问题组织的亲和图法，随后使用定性系统映射来考察主题内部以及主题之间的关系。我们发现，人工智能的相同特性（如扮演角色、响应性和适应性）被父母认为既有潜在用处又令人担忧。父母设想AI可以使基于角色的游戏变得更容易实现。
tldr: 通过对10位美国家长的访谈研究发现，AI在儿童假装游戏中的同一特性（如扮演角色、响应性和适应性）既被家长视为有潜在价值又被视为令人担忧，揭示了家长对AI参与儿童游戏的矛盾态度。
en_tdlr: Interviews with 10 U.S. parents reveal that the same AI characteristics in children's pretend play—such as role assumption, responsiveness, and adaptability—are seen as both potentially useful and concerning, highlighting parents' ambivalent views on AI's role in children's play.
